vo: the person in charge of you
the last time to finish something
a written account of work or results
request permission to be away from work
money you are paid for your job
a piece of work you must do

warm.s: The meeting has been moved to 3 p.m. because our manager is stuck in traffic, so please don't be late this time.
q: Vì sao cuộc họp bị dời?
Why has the meeting been moved?
o: Because the manager is stuck in traffic
Because the meeting room is busy
e: Người nói nói rõ “because our manager is stuck in traffic”. “has been moved to” = đã được dời sang (bị động hiện tại hoàn thành).
The speaker says “because our manager is stuck in traffic”. “has been moved to” is the present perfect passive used to announce a change.

warm.s: I'll send you the report by Friday.
e: “I'll” = I will (lời hứa). “by Friday” = trước/muộn nhất là thứ Sáu – không viết “until Friday”.
“I'll” = I will (a promise). “by Friday” means no later than Friday – don't write “until Friday”.

warm.s: Could you help me with this?
e: Câu yêu cầu lịch sự: Could you + động từ nguyên mẫu. Nhớ “help me with this”, không phải “help me this”.
Polite request: Could you + base verb. Remember “help me with this”, not “help me this”.

warm.s: I have to work overtime twice this week.
e: “work overtime” = tăng ca; “twice” = hai lần. “have to” chỉ sự bắt buộc do hoàn cảnh.
“work overtime” = work extra hours; “twice” = two times. “have to” shows an obligation from the situation.

warm.s: My job involves writing reports, answering emails from clients and organising meetings, so I spend most of the day at my computer.
e: Câu hỏi: What does your job involve? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Chú ý: involve + V-ing.
Question: What does your job involve? – Model answer. Note: involve + -ing.

warm.s: When I feel stressed at work, I make a list of my tasks, take a short walk and ask my colleagues for help if the deadline is too close.
e: Câu hỏi: How do you deal with stress at work? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Nối âm “ask my”, “for help”.
Question: How do you deal with stress at work? – Model answer. Link “ask my” and “for help”.

hard.s: Xin lỗi, tôi bị kẹt với báo cáo này cả buổi sáng – bạn có thể xem qua giúp tôi trước khi tôi gửi cho sếp không?
a: Sorry, I've been stuck on this report all morning – could you have a quick look at it before I send it to the boss?
Sorry, I've been stuck on this report all morning – could you take a quick look at it before I send it to my boss?
Sorry, I've been stuck with this report all morning; could you look over it before I send it to the boss?
Sorry, I've been stuck on this report all morning. Could you look it over before I send it to my manager?
e: “be stuck on/with” = bị bí, kẹt; “have/take a quick look at” hoặc “look it over” = xem qua – cách nói tự nhiên hơn “check”.
“be stuck on/with” = unable to make progress; “have/take a quick look at” or “look it over” sound more natural than “check”.
f: have a quick look at it

q: Viết lại lời từ chối tăng ca cho mềm mỏng hơn, bắt đầu bằng “I'm afraid …”.
Rewrite this refusal to work overtime more politely, starting with “I'm afraid …”.
hard.s: I can't stay late tonight because I have to pick up my son.
a: I'm afraid I can't stay late tonight because I have to pick up my son.
I'm afraid I won't be able to stay late tonight because I have to pick up my son.
I'm afraid I can't stay late tonight, as I have to pick up my son.
e: “I'm afraid …” làm mềm lời từ chối; “won't be able to” còn lịch sự hơn “can't”. “pick up” = đón.
“I'm afraid …” softens a refusal; “won't be able to” is even softer than “can't”. “pick up” = collect someone.
f: I'm afraid I can't stay late

hard.s: Our manager told us that the deadline has been pushed back and we would have another week to finish the project.
a: Our manager told us that the deadline had been pushed back and we would have another week to finish the project.
Our manager told us that the deadline had been pushed back and that we would have another week to finish the project.
e: Câu tường thuật sau “told us that” lùi thì: has been → had been. “push back” = dời lùi (hạn chót).
Reported speech after “told us that” backshifts: has been → had been. “push back” = postpone.

hard.s: I'm totally snowed ___ with emails this week, so would you mind covering the client call for me on Thursday?
a: under
e: “be snowed under (with)” = ngập đầu công việc – thành ngữ rất hay dùng ở văn phòng. Không dùng “snowed in” (bị tuyết chặn).
“be snowed under (with)” = have too much work – a common office idiom. “snowed in” means trapped by snow.

rd2.tx:
Subject: Notes from Monday's meeting

Hi team,

Thanks for coming to this morning's meeting. Here is a short summary. First, the deadline for the Green Park project has been moved to 28 March, so we have two more weeks. Second, Lan is going to write the monthly report, and she will send it to everyone by Friday. Third, because the client wants more changes, some of us will have to work overtime next week. I know this is not easy, so you can take a day off later if you need it. If you want to ask for leave, please tell me at least three days before. Finally, our next meeting will be on Thursday at 3 pm in Room 4. Could you read the new task list before then? And would you mind replying to this email if anything is unclear?

Best wishes,
Minh
Project Manager
rd2.tr:
Tiêu đề: Ghi chú cuộc họp thứ Hai

Cảm ơn mọi người đã đến cuộc họp sáng nay. Đây là phần tóm tắt ngắn. Thứ nhất, hạn chót của dự án Green Park đã được dời sang ngày 28 tháng 3, nên chúng ta có thêm hai tuần. Thứ hai, Lan sẽ viết báo cáo tháng và sẽ gửi cho mọi người trước thứ Sáu. Thứ ba, vì khách hàng muốn sửa thêm, một số người trong chúng ta sẽ phải tăng ca vào tuần tới. Tôi biết điều này không dễ, nên sau đó các bạn có thể nghỉ một ngày nếu cần. Nếu muốn xin nghỉ phép, hãy báo tôi ít nhất ba ngày trước. Cuối cùng, cuộc họp tới sẽ vào thứ Năm lúc 3 giờ chiều ở Phòng 4. Các bạn đọc danh sách nhiệm vụ mới trước đó nhé? Và phiền các bạn trả lời email này nếu có gì chưa rõ.

Thân,
Minh
Quản lý dự án

q: Vì sao nhóm có thêm hai tuần?
Why does the team have two more weeks?
o: Vì hạn chót đã được dời sang 28/3
Because the deadline has been moved to 28 March
Vì khách hàng hủy dự án
Because the client cancelled the project
Vì Lan đã viết xong báo cáo
Because Lan has finished the report
e: Email viết: “the deadline … has been moved to 28 March, so we have two more weeks”. Khách hàng không hủy mà còn muốn sửa thêm.
The email says “the deadline … has been moved to 28 March, so we have two more weeks”. The client did not cancel; it wants more changes.

q: Ai sẽ viết báo cáo tháng?
Who will write the monthly report?
e: “Lan is going to write the monthly report” – be going to diễn tả kế hoạch đã quyết định trong cuộc họp. Minh là người viết email.
“Lan is going to write the monthly report” – be going to shows a plan decided in the meeting. Minh is the writer of the email.

q: Muốn xin nghỉ phép thì phải báo trước bao lâu?
How early must you tell Minh if you want leave?
e: “please tell me at least three days before”. Thứ Năm là ngày họp tiếp theo, không liên quan đến nghỉ phép.
“please tell me at least three days before”. Thursday is the next meeting, not the leave rule.

ex2.s: Don't worry about the client's file – I ___ send it today before I leave the office.
a: will
'll
e: Quyết định ngay lúc nói → will. Không dùng “am going to” vì đây không phải kế hoạch có từ trước.
A decision made at the moment of speaking → will. “am going to” would suggest an earlier plan.

ex2.s: Would you mind ___ the window? It's really hot in the meeting room this afternoon. (open)
a: opening
e: Would you mind + V-ing. Lỗi thường gặp: “mind to open” hoặc “mind open”.
Would you mind + -ing form. Common mistakes: “mind to open” or “mind open”.

ex2.s: The meeting has been moved ___ Friday because the manager is visiting a client on Thursday.
a: to
e: move something to + thời gian mới: dời sang. Không dùng “on” sau “moved” trong nghĩa này.
move something to + the new time. Don't use “on” after “moved” here.

ex2.s: I've already booked my train tickets, so I ___ take two days off next week to visit my parents in Hue.
e: Vé đã đặt → kế hoạch có từ trước → be going to. “will” dùng cho quyết định tức thời; “going to” thiếu động từ be.
The tickets are already booked → an existing plan → be going to. “will” is for instant decisions; “going to” alone is missing “am”.

ex2.s: Next month we will going to start a new project with a big client from Singapore, so everyone in the team is excited.
a: Next month we are going to start a new project with a big client from Singapore, so everyone in the team is excited.
Next month we're going to start a new project with a big client from Singapore, so everyone in the team is excited.
e: Không ghép “will” với “going to”. Kế hoạch đã có → are going to (hoặc will start).
Never combine “will” and “going to”. For a plan, use are going to (or will start).

ex2.s: Would you mind to check my report before I send it to the manager at the end of this afternoon?
a: Would you mind checking my report before I send it to the manager at the end of this afternoon?
e: Sau “mind” luôn là V-ing: mind checking. “mind to check” là lỗi rất phổ biến của người Việt.
“mind” is always followed by -ing: mind checking. “mind to check” is a very common mistake.

q: Viết lại thành yêu cầu lịch sự bắt đầu bằng “Could you …?”
Rewrite as a polite request beginning with “Could you …?”
ex2.s: Send me the sales report before the meeting on Thursday afternoon.
a: Could you send me the sales report before the meeting on Thursday afternoon?
Could you please send me the sales report before the meeting on Thursday afternoon?
Could you send me the sales report before the meeting on Thursday afternoon, please?
e: Could you + động từ nguyên mẫu, đổi dấu chấm thành dấu hỏi. Câu mệnh lệnh trực tiếp nghe khá cộc với đồng nghiệp.
Could you + base verb, ending with a question mark. A direct command can sound rude to colleagues.

ex2.s: Tôi đang bận, lát nữa tôi gọi lại nhé.
a: I'm busy right now; I'll call you back later.
I'm busy right now, I'll call you back later.
I'm busy right now. I'll call you back later.
I am busy right now; I will call you back later.
I'm busy at the moment; I'll call you back later.
e: Quyết định ngay lúc nói → I'll. “call you back” = gọi lại; đừng quên “back”.
An instant decision → I'll. “call you back” = return the call; don't forget “back”.

ex2.s: Ai phụ trách dự án này?
a: Who is in charge of this project?
Who's in charge of this project?
Who is responsible for this project?
Who's responsible for this project?
e: “be in charge of” = phụ trách. Câu hỏi với Who làm chủ ngữ nên không cần trợ động từ “does”.
“be in charge of” = be responsible for. Who is the subject, so no “does” is needed.

ex2.s: Nếu bạn muốn xin nghỉ phép, hãy báo cho sếp ít nhất ba ngày trước.
a: If you want to ask for leave, please tell your boss at least three days before.
If you want to ask for leave, please tell your boss at least three days in advance.
If you want to ask for leave, tell your boss at least three days in advance.
If you want to ask for leave, please tell your manager at least three days in advance.
e: “ask for leave” = xin nghỉ phép; “in advance/before” = trước. Không viết “tell to your boss”.
“ask for leave” = request time off; “in advance/before” = earlier. Don't write “tell to your boss”.

ex2.s: I have to|work overtime|twice this week|because the deadline|for the new project|has been moved|to Friday
m: Tuần này tôi phải tăng ca hai lần vì hạn chót của dự án mới đã bị dời lên thứ Sáu.
I have to work overtime twice this week because the deadline for the new project has been moved to Friday.
e: Trật tự: chủ ngữ + have to + động từ + tần suất/thời gian, rồi mệnh đề lý do “because …”.
Order: subject + have to + verb + frequency/time, then the reason clause “because …”.

q: Viết biên bản một cuộc họp tưởng tượng khoảng 120 từ: ngày giờ, người tham dự, 3 quyết định, việc cần làm và người phụ trách.
Write the minutes of an imaginary meeting (about 120 words): date and time, attendees, 3 decisions, actions and who is responsible.
ex2.m:
Meeting minutes – Marketing team
Date: Tuesday 12 May, 9:00–10:00
Attendees: Ms Hoa (manager), Nam, Linh, Duc

Decisions:
1. The summer campaign will start on 1 June, not 15 June, because the client wants it earlier.
2. The team is going to use a new design for the website banner.
3. The budget for online ads has been increased by ten percent.

**Ngữ pháp 1 – tính từ đuôi -ed và -ing**
• **-ed** = cảm xúc của người: I'm **bored**. She was **embarrassed**. We felt **exhausted**.
• **-ing** = tính chất của sự việc/người gây ra cảm xúc: The film is **boring**. It was an **embarrassing** moment.
• Ví dụ: The lesson was **confusing**, so I was **confused**. / He's **interesting**, so I'm **interested** in his stories.
• Lỗi rất hay gặp: “I'm boring” (= tôi là người nhàm chán!) thay vì “I'm bored”.

**Grammar 1 – -ed and -ing adjectives**
• **-ed** = how a person feels: I'm **bored**. She was **embarrassed**. We felt **exhausted**.
• **-ing** = the thing or person that causes the feeling: The film is **boring**. It was an **embarrassing** moment.
• Examples: The lesson was **confusing**, so I was **confused**. / He's **interesting**, so I'm **interested** in his stories.
• Very common mistake: “I'm boring” (= I am a boring person!) instead of “I'm bored”.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – make / feel / seem + tính từ**
• **make sb + adj**: Loud music makes me nervous. Her jokes always make me laugh (make + V).
• **feel / seem / look + adj** (không dùng trạng từ): You seem worried. I feel a bit lonely.
• Mô tả tính cách: She's **outgoing** and **generous**, but she **tends to** be a bit impatient.
• Làm mềm nhận xét tiêu cực: a bit, quite, rather; He can be a bit selfish sometimes.

**Grammar 2 – make / feel / seem + adjective**
• **make sb + adj**: Loud music makes me nervous. Her jokes always make me laugh (make + verb).
• **feel / seem / look + adjective** (not an adverb): You seem worried. I feel a bit lonely.
• Describing personality: She's **outgoing** and **generous**, but she **tends to** be a bit impatient.
• Softening negative comments: a bit, quite, rather; He can be a bit selfish sometimes.

**Phát âm**
• Đuôi -ed của tính từ: bored /d/, relaxed /t/, excited /ɪd/, frustrated /ɪd/, embarrassed /t/.
• Trọng âm: **CON**fident, **GEN**erous, am**BI**tious, re**LI**able, **SEN**sitive, **HON**est (h câm).
• Ngữ điệu thể hiện cảm xúc: nói “I'm fine.” xuống giọng nhanh nghe như đang buồn/khó chịu.

**Pronunciation**
• The -ed ending in adjectives: bored /d/, relaxed /t/, excited /ɪd/, frustrated /ɪd/, embarrassed /t/.
• Word stress: **CON**fident, **GEN**erous, am**BI**tious, re**LI**able, **SEN**sitive, **HON**est (silent h).
• Intonation carries feelings: a quick, falling “I'm fine.” can sound upset or annoyed.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe 1 podcast/video ngắn về tính cách (introvert vs extrovert), ghi 8 tính từ.
• Nói (20 phút): mô tả tính cách 2 người bạn thân trong 2 phút, dùng ví dụ cụ thể (She's generous – she always …).
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 2 thư hỏi đáp tâm sự (advice column), gạch chân tính từ cảm xúc.
• Viết (30 phút): viết nhật ký cảm xúc 100–120 từ về một ngày gần đây: chuyện gì xảy ra, bạn cảm thấy thế nào, vì sao.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học 10 cặp tính từ trái nghĩa: shy – outgoing, patient – impatient, generous – mean, honest – dishonest, calm – anxious …

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): listen to a short podcast or video about personality (introverts vs extroverts); note 8 adjectives.
• Speaking (20 min): describe 2 close friends' personalities for 2 minutes with real examples (She's generous – she always …).
• Reading (20 min): read 2 advice-column letters; underline the feeling adjectives.
• Writing (30 min): write a 100–120-word feelings diary about a recent day: what happened, how you felt and why.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn 10 pairs of opposites: shy – outgoing, patient – impatient, generous – mean, honest – dishonest, calm – anxious …

rd2.tx:
Dear Anna,
I need some advice. I've just started university and I share a flat with a girl called Mia. She is very friendly and outgoing, and she always makes me laugh. However, I'm quite shy, and sometimes I feel a bit embarrassed when she invites lots of people home. Last weekend she had a party until two in the morning. I was exhausted and annoyed, but I didn't say anything because I didn't want to seem rude. Now I feel frustrated, and I'm worried that our friendship will get worse. My mum says I should be more honest, but talking about problems makes me nervous. Is it selfish to ask her for some quiet evenings? What should I do?
Thanks,
Lonely in Leeds
rd2.tr:
Chị Anna thân mến,
Em cần một lời khuyên. Em vừa mới vào đại học và ở chung căn hộ với một bạn nữ tên là Mia. Bạn ấy rất thân thiện và hòa đồng, và luôn làm em bật cười. Tuy nhiên, em khá nhút nhát, và đôi khi em thấy hơi ngại khi bạn ấy mời nhiều người về nhà. Cuối tuần trước bạn ấy tổ chức tiệc đến hai giờ sáng. Em kiệt sức và bực mình, nhưng em không nói gì vì không muốn tỏ ra bất lịch sự. Giờ em thấy bức bối, và em lo rằng tình bạn của chúng em sẽ xấu đi. Mẹ em bảo em nên thẳng thắn hơn, nhưng nói về các vấn đề khiến em lo lắng. Đề nghị bạn ấy cho vài buổi tối yên tĩnh có phải là ích kỷ không? Em nên làm gì đây?
Cảm ơn chị,
Cô đơn ở Leeds

It makes me angry when people talk loudly on their phones on the bus.
When people talk loudly on their phones on the bus, it makes me angry.
e: Chủ ngữ là nguyên nhân + make + tân ngữ + tính từ; hoặc “It makes me angry when …”.

q: Viết thư trả lời “Lonely in Leeds” khoảng 120 từ: thể hiện sự thông cảm, nhận xét tình huống, đưa ra 2–3 lời khuyên.
Write a reply to “Lonely in Leeds” (about 120 words): show sympathy, comment on the situation and give 2–3 pieces of advice.
ex2.m:
Dear Lonely in Leeds,
Thank you for your letter. It's completely normal to feel frustrated when you live with someone who is very different from you, so please don't feel guilty. You are not being selfish – everyone needs quiet time, especially at university.
First, I think you should talk to Mia when you are both relaxed, not just after a party. Tell her how you feel and give her a specific example. Second, you could suggest some simple rules, for example no guests after eleven on weekdays. Finally, try joining one of her smaller get-togethers; you might find them less stressful than you expect.
Good luck – I'm sure Mia will understand.
Anna
e: Cần có: câu thể hiện thông cảm (It's normal to feel …); ít nhất 4 tính từ cảm xúc/tính cách dùng đúng -ed/-ing; 2–3 lời khuyên với should/could/try + V-ing; lời kết động viên.
Include: sympathy (It's normal to feel …); at least 4 feeling/personality adjectives with correct -ed/-ing; 2–3 pieces of advice with should/could/try + -ing; an encouraging ending.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Cụm động từ về quan hệ**
• **get on (well) with sb**: hợp với ai: I get on well with my new roommate.
• **fall out (with sb) over sth**: cãi nhau, giận nhau vì việc gì: They fell out over money.
• **make up**: làm lành: We argued, but we made up the next day.
• **catch up (with sb)**: gặp lại để kể chuyện: Let's catch up over coffee.
• **cheer sb up**: làm ai vui lên – tân ngữ là đại từ phải đứng giữa: cheer **me** up (KHÔNG nói “cheer up me”).

**Grammar 1 – Relationship phrasal verbs**
• **get on (well) with sb**: have a good relationship: I get on well with my new roommate.
• **fall out (with sb) over sth**: argue and stop being friendly: They fell out over money.
• **make up**: become friends again: We argued, but we made up the next day.
• **catch up (with sb)**: meet and share news: Let's catch up over coffee.
• **cheer sb up**: make someone happier – a pronoun object goes in the middle: cheer **me** up (NOT “cheer up me”).

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Hiện tại hoàn thành với for / since**
• **for** + khoảng thời gian: I've known Lan **for** ten years.
• **since** + mốc thời gian: We've been friends **since** 2015 / **since** we were at school.
• Hỏi: How long have you known each other? (KHÔNG dùng “How long do you know…”).
• **used to** + V: thói quen/tình trạng trong quá khứ nay không còn: We used to live next door.

**Grammar 2 – Present perfect with for / since**
• **for** + a period: I've known Lan **for** ten years.
• **since** + a starting point: We've been friends **since** 2015 / **since** we were at school.
• Ask: How long have you known each other? (NOT “How long do you know…”).
• **used to** + verb: a past habit or state that is no longer true: We used to live next door.

**Phát âm – Nối âm trong cụm động từ**
• Phụ âm cuối nối với nguyên âm đầu: get‿on /ɡeɾ‿ɑːn/, fell‿out /fe‿laʊt/, make‿up /meɪ‿kʌp/, cheer‿up.
• Trọng âm thường rơi vào **tiểu từ**: We fell OUT. / They made UP.
• **used to** đọc /ˈjuːs.tə/, không đọc /juːzd tuː/.

**Pronunciation – Linking in phrasal verbs**
• A final consonant links to the next vowel: get‿on /ɡeɾ‿ɑːn/, fell‿out /fe‿laʊt/, make‿up /meɪ‿kʌp/, cheer‿up.
• The stress usually falls on the **particle**: We fell OUT. / They made UP.
• **used to** is pronounced /ˈjuːs.tə/, not /juːzd tuː/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): xem 1 cảnh phim/sitcom về tình bạn, ghi lại 5 cụm động từ nghe được.
• Nói (20 phút): kể 2 phút về người bạn thân nhất: quen từ khi nào, vì sao hợp nhau, từng giận nhau chưa.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 1 bài tư vấn tình bạn (advice column), tóm tắt lời khuyên trong 3 câu.
• Viết (30 phút): viết email 100–120 từ cho một người bạn cũ đã lâu không liên lạc.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): làm thẻ cho 10 cụm động từ trong bài, mỗi thẻ 1 câu về bản thân.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): watch one scene from a film or sitcom about friendship and note 5 phrasal verbs.
• Speaking (20 min): talk for 2 minutes about your best friend: how long you've known them, why you get on, whether you've ever fallen out.
• Reading (20 min): read an advice column about friendship and sum up the advice in 3 sentences.
• Writing (30 min): write a 100–120-word email to an old friend you haven't contacted for a long time.
• Vocabulary (15 min): make cards for the 10 phrasal verbs in this unit, each with one sentence about yourself.

e: Nhấn mạnh “YEARS” và “catching UP”; “looking forward to” + V-ing.
Stress “YEARS” and “catching UP”; “looking forward to” + -ing.

hard.s: Thật ra tụi mình không hẳn là giận nhau đâu – chỉ là dạo này mỗi đứa một việc nên dần dần ít liên lạc thôi.
a: We didn't really fall out – we've just been busy with our own lives lately, so we've gradually drifted apart.
We didn't actually fall out – we've just both been busy lately, so we've slowly drifted apart.
We haven't really fallen out – we've just been busy with our own things lately, so we've gradually lost touch.
We didn't really fall out – we've both just been so busy lately that we've gradually lost touch.
e: “dần dần ít liên lạc” = **drift apart** hoặc **lose touch** (B2). Dùng hiện tại hoàn thành vì tình trạng kéo dài đến nay.
“dần dần ít liên lạc” = **drift apart** or **lose touch** (B2). Use the present perfect because the situation continues now.

q: Viết lại thành lời trách nhẹ nhàng, lịch sự dùng “I wish you'd…”.
Rewrite as a gentle, polite complaint using “I wish you'd…”.
hard.s: You borrowed my charger without asking me again, and it really annoys me.
a: I wish you'd ask me before you borrow my charger.
I wish you'd ask before borrowing my charger.
I wish you would ask me before you borrow my charger.
I wish you'd ask me first before borrowing my charger.
e: **I wish you'd + V** dùng để phàn nàn nhẹ nhàng về thói quen của người khác – lịch sự hơn nhiều so với “it annoys me”.
**I wish you'd + verb** softly complains about someone's habit – much more polite than “it annoys me”.

hard.s: She told me she's sorry about last night and that she didn't mean hurting my feelings, so I've decided to let it go.
a: She told me she's sorry about last night and that she didn't mean to hurt my feelings, so I've decided to let it go.
She told me she was sorry about last night and that she didn't mean to hurt my feelings, so I've decided to let it go.
e: “không cố ý làm gì” = **didn't mean to + V**. “mean + V-ing” lại có nghĩa “dẫn đến/bao hàm”, không hợp ở đây.
“not intend to do something” = **didn't mean to + verb**. “mean + -ing” means “involve”, which doesn't fit here.

hard.s: Don't worry about Minh – he's upset now, but he never holds a ___ for long, so I'm sure you two will be fine by the weekend.
a: grudge
e: **hold a grudge** = để bụng, thù dai. Đây là cụm cố định thường gặp khi nói về cãi nhau giữa bạn bè.
**hold a grudge** = stay angry with someone for a long time. A very common fixed phrase about arguments.

rd2.tx:
Hi Lan,
It's been ages since we last caught up! I've been really busy since I moved to Da Nang, but I think about you a lot. Do you remember Minh, my roommate? We used to get on really well, but last month we fell out over something silly: he borrowed my laptop without asking and broke the charger. We didn't speak for a week. In the end, he apologised and offered to buy a new one, so we made up. Honestly, I've learned that good friends don't have to agree about everything; they just have to be honest with each other. I've also joined a hiking club, and I've already made two new friends there. They're the kind of people who always cheer you up. Anyway, let's meet up when you visit in December. I can't wait to hear all your news!
Love,
Hoa
rd2.tr:
Chào Lan,
Lâu lắm rồi chúng mình chưa gặp nhau hàn huyên! Từ khi chuyển đến Đà Nẵng mình rất bận, nhưng mình nghĩ về bạn nhiều lắm. Bạn còn nhớ Minh, bạn cùng phòng của mình không? Trước đây bọn mình rất hợp nhau, nhưng tháng trước bọn mình giận nhau vì một chuyện vớ vẩn: cậu ấy mượn laptop của mình mà không hỏi và làm hỏng bộ sạc. Bọn mình không nói chuyện với nhau suốt một tuần. Cuối cùng cậu ấy xin lỗi và đề nghị mua cái mới, thế là bọn mình làm lành. Thật lòng, mình đã học được rằng bạn tốt không cần phải đồng ý với nhau mọi chuyện; chỉ cần thành thật với nhau thôi. Mình cũng tham gia một câu lạc bộ leo núi và đã có thêm hai người bạn mới ở đó. Họ là kiểu người luôn làm mình vui lên. Mà thôi, khi bạn đến chơi vào tháng Mười Hai thì mình gặp nhau nhé. Mình nóng lòng muốn nghe hết tin tức của bạn!
Thương,
Hoa

q: Vì sao Hoa và Minh giận nhau?
Why did Hoa and Minh fall out?
o: Minh mượn laptop không hỏi và làm hỏng bộ sạc
Minh borrowed her laptop without asking and broke the charger
e: Câu “he borrowed my laptop without asking and broke the charger” nêu rõ lý do.
The sentence “he borrowed my laptop without asking and broke the charger” gives the reason.
f: he borrowed my laptop without asking

q: Họ làm lành như thế nào?
How did they make up?
o: Minh xin lỗi và đề nghị mua bộ sạc mới
Minh apologised and offered to buy a new one
Một người bạn giúp họ nói chuyện
e: “he apologised and offered to buy a new one, so we made up” – Minh là người xin lỗi.
“he apologised and offered to buy a new one, so we made up” – it was Minh who apologised.
f: he apologised and offered to buy a new one

q: Theo Hoa, bạn tốt cần điều gì?
According to Hoa, what do good friends need?
o: To be honest with each other
Đồng ý với nhau mọi chuyện
e: Hoa viết bạn tốt “don't have to agree about everything; they just have to be honest with each other”. Phương án 2 là bẫy – trái ngược với bài.
Hoa says good friends “don't have to agree about everything; they just have to be honest”. Option 2 is the trap – it says the opposite.

ex2.s: Even though we now live in different countries, my best friend and I have stayed close because we ___ in touch through video calls every weekend.
e: Cụm cố định là **keep in touch** (giữ liên lạc). “hold in touch” không tồn tại; “stay in touch” đúng nhưng “stay on in touch” thì sai.
The fixed phrase is **keep in touch**. “hold in touch” does not exist; “stay in touch” is fine but “stay on in touch” is wrong.

ex2.s: Nam and his roommate ___ out over the electricity bill last month, but they have finally sorted out the problem and are friends again.
a: fell
e: “last month” → quá khứ đơn: **fell out** (fall – fell – fallen) = giận nhau, cãi nhau.
“last month” needs the past simple: **fell out** (fall – fell – fallen) = argued and stopped being friendly.

ex2.s: I have known Linh since five years, and in all that time she has never let me down or told anyone my secrets.
a: I have known Linh for five years, and in all that time she has never let me down or told anyone my secrets.
I've known Linh for five years, and in all that time she has never let me down or told anyone my secrets.
I've known Linh for five years, and in all that time she's never let me down or told anyone my secrets.
e: “five years” là khoảng thời gian → dùng **for**. **since** chỉ đi với mốc: since 2020, since school.
“five years” is a period, so use **for**. **since** goes with a starting point: since 2020, since school.

ex2.s: My new colleagues are really friendly and helpful, so I get on well to all of them and we often have lunch together.
a: My new colleagues are really friendly and helpful, so I get on well with all of them and we often have lunch together.
e: Cụm đúng là **get on well with** sb. Người Việt hay dùng “to” vì nghĩ “hợp với” = “to”.
The phrase is **get on well with** someone. Learners often use “to” by translating word for word.

ex2.s: When I failed my driving test, my sister took me out for ice cream and told funny stories to cheer up me.
a: When I failed my driving test, my sister took me out for ice cream and told funny stories to cheer me up.
e: Với cụm động từ tách được, đại từ tân ngữ (me, him, her…) phải đứng **giữa**: cheer **me** up, không nói “cheer up me”.
With separable phrasal verbs, an object pronoun must go **in the middle**: cheer **me** up, not “cheer up me”.

ex2.s: Tôi đã quen Mai được mười năm, và cô ấy là người duy nhất tôi có thể tin tưởng hoàn toàn.
a: I have known Mai for ten years, and she is the only person I can trust completely.
I've known Mai for ten years, and she's the only person I can trust completely.
I've known Mai for ten years, and she is the only person I can completely trust.
I have known Mai for ten years, and she is the only person I can totally trust.
e: “đã quen… được mười năm” = hiện tại hoàn thành + for: **I have known… for ten years**. Không dùng “I know Mai for ten years”.
“đã quen… được mười năm” needs the present perfect + for: **I have known… for ten years**, not “I know Mai for ten years”.
f: I have known Mai for ten years

ex2.s: Khi tôi buồn, bạn thân của tôi luôn gọi điện và làm tôi vui lên bằng những câu chuyện hài hước.
a: When I am sad, my best friend always calls me and cheers me up with funny stories.
When I'm sad, my best friend always calls me and cheers me up with funny stories.
When I feel sad, my best friend always calls me and cheers me up with funny stories.
When I'm feeling down, my best friend always calls me and cheers me up with funny stories.
When I feel down, my best friend always calls me and cheers me up with funny stories.
e: “làm tôi vui lên” = **cheer me up**; chủ ngữ ngôi ba số ít → **calls**, **cheers**.
“làm tôi vui lên” = **cheer me up**; with a third-person singular subject use **calls**, **cheers**.

q: Viết lại câu bằng hiện tại hoàn thành với “since”.
Rewrite the sentence using the present perfect with “since”.
ex2.s: Tom and I became friends in 2015 when we joined the same football team, and we are still friends today.
a: Tom and I have been friends since 2015, when we joined the same football team.
Tom and I have been friends since we joined the same football team in 2015.
Tom and I've been friends since 2015, when we joined the same football team.
e: Hành động bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn còn → **have been friends since** + mốc (2015 / we joined…).
A situation that started in the past and is still true → **have been friends since** + a starting point.

ex2.s: Although we fell out|over a silly misunderstanding,|we both apologised|to each other|and have been|even closer|ever since.
m: Mặc dù chúng tôi giận nhau vì một hiểu lầm ngớ ngẩn, cả hai đã xin lỗi nhau và từ đó đến giờ còn thân hơn.
Although we fell out over a silly misunderstanding, we both apologised to each other and have been even closer ever since.
e: “fall out over + việc”; “ever since” (từ đó đến giờ) đi với hiện tại hoàn thành “have been”.
“fall out over + something”; “ever since” goes with the present perfect “have been”.

q: Viết email (80–100 từ) cho một người bạn cũ lâu ngày không gặp: kể tin mới, nhắc một kỷ niệm và hẹn gặp.
Write an email (80–100 words) to an old friend you haven't seen for a long time: share news, mention a memory and suggest meeting up.
ex2.m:
Hi Nam,
It's been ages since we last caught up! I've been working in Hanoi since March, and I've finally got used to the traffic. Do you remember the summer we used to ride our bikes to the beach every morning? I still laugh about the day you fell into the sea with your phone in your pocket. I've made some great friends here, but nobody makes me laugh like you do. Are you free at the end of the month? Let's meet up for coffee and catch up properly.
Take care,
Huy
e: Cần có: lời chào thân mật; ít nhất 2 câu hiện tại hoàn thành (for/since); 1 kỷ niệm với “used to”; lời hẹn gặp với cụm động từ (meet up, catch up).
Include: a friendly greeting; at least 2 present perfect sentences (for/since); one memory with “used to”; an invitation using phrasal verbs (meet up, catch up).

t: Ngân hàng, bưu điện & thủ tục
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Câu bị động trong thủ tục**
• Hiện tại đơn: **is/are + V3**: International transfers **are charged** at 2%.
• Quá khứ đơn: **was/were + V3**: My parcel **was sent** last Monday.
• Với động từ khuyết thiếu: **must/will/can + be + V3**: The form **must be signed** here. / Your card **will be sent** by post.
• Dùng bị động khi việc làm quan trọng hơn người làm – rất phổ biến trong thông báo, biểu mẫu.

**Grammar 1 – The passive in paperwork**
• Present simple: **is/are + past participle**: International transfers **are charged** at 2%.
• Past simple: **was/were + past participle**: My parcel **was sent** last Monday.
• With modals: **must/will/can + be + past participle**: The form **must be signed** here. / Your card **will be sent** by post.
• Use the passive when the action matters more than who does it – very common in notices and forms.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Yêu cầu & câu hỏi lịch sự**
• **I'd like to** + V: I'd like to open an account.
• **Could you** + V…?: Could you check my balance, please?
• **Would it be possible to** + V…? (rất lịch sự)
• Câu hỏi gián tiếp – KHÔNG đảo ngữ: Could you tell me **where I can** withdraw cash? (không nói “where can I”).

**Grammar 2 – Polite requests & questions**
• **I'd like to** + verb: I'd like to open an account.
• **Could you** + verb…?: Could you check my balance, please?
• **Would it be possible to** + verb…? (very polite)
• Indirect questions – NO inversion: Could you tell me **where I can** withdraw cash? (not “where can I”).

**Phát âm – Số, ngày tháng & đuôi -tion**
• Phân biệt trọng âm: thir**TEEN** /θɝːˈtiːn/ ↔ **THIR**ty /ˈθɝː.t̬i/; fif**TEEN** ↔ **FIF**ty.
• Ngày tháng: “the fifth of May” / “May fifth” – nhớ âm /θ/ cuối.
• Từ đuôi **-tion** nhấn âm ngay trước nó: appli**CA**tion, identifi**CA**tion, transac**TION** → trans**AC**tion.
• Đánh vần tên: luyện bảng chữ cái, đặc biệt G /dʒiː/ – J /dʒeɪ/, E /iː/ – I /aɪ/.

**Pronunciation – Numbers, dates & -tion words**
• Contrast the stress: thir**TEEN** /θɝːˈtiːn/ ↔ **THIR**ty /ˈθɝː.t̬i/; fif**TEEN** ↔ **FIF**ty.
• Dates: “the fifth of May” / “May fifth” – pronounce the final /θ/.
• Words ending in **-tion** stress the syllable just before it: appli**CA**tion, identifi**CA**tion, trans**AC**tion.
• Spelling names: practise the alphabet, especially G /dʒiː/ – J /dʒeɪ/, E /iː/ – I /aɪ/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (20 phút): nghe 2 hội thoại mẫu ở ngân hàng/bưu điện, ghi lại số tiền, ngày, mã số.
• Nói (20 phút): đóng vai khách hàng: mở tài khoản, gửi bưu kiện, báo mất thẻ – mỗi tình huống 1 phút.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc điều khoản phí trên website một ngân hàng, gạch chân 10 câu bị động.
• Viết (30 phút): điền 1 mẫu đơn tiếng Anh (thông tin giả) và viết email 80–100 từ báo mất thẻ.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học 15 từ về tiền và giấy tờ (balance, receipt, proof of address…).

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (20 min): listen to 2 sample dialogues at a bank or post office and note the amounts, dates and numbers.
• Speaking (20 min): role-play as a customer: opening an account, sending a parcel, reporting a lost card – 1 minute each.
• Reading (20 min): read the fees page of a bank's website and underline 10 passive sentences.
• Writing (30 min): fill in an English form (with made-up details) and write an 80–100-word email reporting a lost card.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn 15 words about money and documents (balance, receipt, proof of address…).

warm.s: Your new bank card will be sent to your home address by post, but the PIN will arrive separately a few days later for security reasons.
q: Mã PIN sẽ đến như thế nào?
How will the PIN arrive?
o: It must be collected at the bank
e: “the PIN will arrive separately a few days later” – gửi riêng để đảm bảo an toàn.
“the PIN will arrive separately a few days later” – it is sent separately for security.

warm.s: Could you tell me how much it costs to send this parcel to Australia by airmail?
e: Câu hỏi gián tiếp: “how much it costs” (không đảo “does it cost”). “airmail” viết liền.
Indirect question: “how much it costs” (no “does it cost”). “airmail” is one word.

warm.s: Excuse me, I'd like to change two hundred US dollars into Vietnamese dong, please. What's today's exchange rate?
e: Nối âm “I'd‿like”, nhấn “exCHANGE rate”. Lên giọng nhẹ ở cuối câu hỏi lịch sự.
Link “I'd‿like”, stress “exCHANGE rate”. Use a gentle rise in the polite question.

warm.s: I'm afraid I've lost my bank card, so could you block it and send me a new one as soon as possible?
e: “I'm afraid” làm câu báo tin xấu mềm hơn. Nối âm “block‿it”, “send‿me”.
“I'm afraid” softens bad news. Link “block‿it” and “send‿me”.

hard.s: Tôi e là có nhầm lẫn gì đó – tôi bị trừ phí hai lần cho cùng một giao dịch.
a: I'm afraid there's been a mistake – I've been charged twice for the same transaction.
I'm afraid there has been a mistake – I have been charged twice for the same transaction.
I'm afraid there's been some mistake – I've been charged twice for the same transaction.
I'm afraid there's been a mistake – I was charged twice for the same transaction.
e: Phàn nàn lịch sự bắt đầu bằng **I'm afraid…**. “bị trừ phí” = bị động hiện tại hoàn thành **I've been charged**.
A polite complaint starts with **I'm afraid…**. “bị trừ phí” = present perfect passive **I've been charged**.

q: Chuyển sang lời gián tiếp: bắt đầu bằng “She asked the clerk…”.
Report the question, starting with “She asked the clerk…”.
hard.s: “Where can I pick up my parcel if I'm not at home when it's delivered?” she asked the clerk.
a: She asked the clerk where she could pick up her parcel if she wasn't at home when it was delivered.
She asked the clerk where she could pick up her parcel if she was not at home when it was delivered.
She asked the clerk where she could pick her parcel up if she wasn't at home when it was delivered.
e: Câu hỏi tường thuật: lùi thì (can → could, am → was, is → was), đổi đại từ (my → her) và KHÔNG đảo ngữ: **where she could pick up**.
Reported questions: backshift (can → could, am → was, is → was), change pronouns (my → her) and use NO inversion: **where she could pick up**.
f: where she could pick up her parcel

hard.s: I'd like to make a complaint about my parcel, which was arrived badly damaged even though the box was clearly marked as fragile.
a: I'd like to make a complaint about my parcel, which arrived badly damaged even though the box was clearly marked as fragile.
I would like to make a complaint about my parcel, which arrived badly damaged even though the box was clearly marked as fragile.
e: **arrive** là nội động từ – không có bị động. Viết **which arrived damaged**; “was marked” thì đúng vì hộp được người khác ghi nhãn.
**arrive** is intransitive and has no passive: **which arrived damaged**. “was marked” is correct because someone marked the box.

hard.s: If I ___ known how high the fee was going to be, I would have transferred the money through the app instead of queuing at the bank.
a: had
'd
e: Điều kiện loại 3 (tiếc nuối quá khứ): **If + had + V3, would have + V3** → If I **had** known…
Third conditional (regret about the past): **If + had + past participle, would have + past participle** → If I **had** known…

rd2.tx:
Clerk: Good morning. How can I help you?
Linh: Hi, I'd like to open a savings account, please.
Clerk: Of course. Could I see your passport or ID card?
Linh: Here you are. I've just moved here, so the address on my ID hasn't been updated yet.
Clerk: That's fine, but you'll need to bring a utility bill with your new address. The form must be signed here and here.
Linh: Sure. How long does it take to get the bank card?
Clerk: The card is usually sent by post within five working days. Your PIN is sent separately for security reasons.
Linh: Great. One more thing – I also need to send some money to my parents abroad. Is there a fee?
Clerk: Yes, international transfers are charged at two percent. You can also do it in our app, which is cheaper.
Linh: Thanks, that's really helpful.
rd2.tr:
Nhân viên: Chào buổi sáng. Tôi có thể giúp gì cho chị?
Linh: Chào anh, tôi muốn mở một tài khoản tiết kiệm.
Nhân viên: Vâng. Cho tôi xem hộ chiếu hoặc căn cước của chị được không?
Linh: Đây ạ. Tôi vừa chuyển đến đây nên địa chỉ trên căn cước chưa được cập nhật.
Nhân viên: Không sao, nhưng chị sẽ cần mang một hóa đơn điện nước có địa chỉ mới. Mẫu đơn phải được ký ở đây và ở đây.
Linh: Vâng. Mất bao lâu thì tôi nhận được thẻ ngân hàng?
Nhân viên: Thẻ thường được gửi qua bưu điện trong vòng năm ngày làm việc. Mã PIN được gửi riêng vì lý do bảo mật.
Linh: Tốt quá. Còn một việc nữa – tôi cũng cần gửi ít tiền cho bố mẹ ở nước ngoài. Có mất phí không?

q: Cách gửi tiền ra nước ngoài nào rẻ hơn?
Which way of sending money abroad is cheaper?

Gửi tiền mặt qua bưu điện

ex2.s: Before your passport application can be processed, the form must ___ in black ink and signed at the bottom of the second page.
e: Sau **must** dùng bị động **be + V3**: must **be filled in**. Lá đơn không tự điền nên không dùng chủ động “fill in”.
After **must**, the passive is **be + past participle**: must **be filled in**. The form doesn't fill itself, so active “fill in” is wrong.

ex2.s: My parcel ___ (send) from Hanoi last Monday, but according to the tracking website it still hasn't arrived in Ho Chi Minh City.
a: was sent
e: Gói hàng được gửi (bị động) + “last Monday” (quá khứ) → **was sent**.
The parcel receives the action (passive) + “last Monday” (past) → **was sent**.

ex2.s: Excuse me, could you tell me where can I withdraw some cash, because the machine outside the bank isn't working today?
a: Excuse me, could you tell me where I can withdraw some cash, because the machine outside the bank isn't working today?
e: Câu hỏi gián tiếp sau “could you tell me” giữ trật tự câu khẳng định: **where I can**, không đảo “where can I”.
An indirect question after “could you tell me” uses statement word order: **where I can**, not “where can I”.

ex2.s: All international transfers is charged a small fee, so many students prefer to send money home through the bank's mobile app.
a: All international transfers are charged a small fee, so many students prefer to send money home through the bank's mobile app.
e: Chủ ngữ số nhiều “transfers” → bị động **are charged**. Đừng để “fee” số ít đánh lừa.
The plural subject “transfers” needs **are charged**. Don't be misled by the singular “fee”.

ex2.s: Tôi muốn mở một tài khoản tiết kiệm, nhưng tôi không chắc mình cần mang theo những giấy tờ gì.
a: I'd like to open a savings account, but I'm not sure what documents I need to bring.
I would like to open a savings account, but I'm not sure what documents I need to bring.
I'd like to open a savings account, but I'm not sure which documents I need to bring.
I'd like to open a savings account, but I am not sure what documents I need to bring with me.
e: “Tôi muốn” lịch sự = **I'd like to**. “những giấy tờ gì” là câu hỏi gián tiếp: **what documents I need** (không có “do”).
Polite “tôi muốn” = **I'd like to**. “những giấy tờ gì” is an indirect question: **what documents I need** (no “do”).

ex2.s: Gói hàng của bạn sẽ được giao trong vòng ba ngày làm việc, và bạn sẽ nhận được tin nhắn khi nó đến.
a: Your parcel will be delivered within three working days, and you will receive a text message when it arrives.
Your parcel will be delivered within three working days, and you'll receive a text message when it arrives.
Your parcel will be delivered within three working days, and you'll get a message when it arrives.
Your package will be delivered within three working days, and you'll get a text when it arrives.
e: “sẽ được giao” = **will be delivered**. Sau “when” nói về tương lai dùng hiện tại đơn: **when it arrives** (không “will arrive”).
“sẽ được giao” = **will be delivered**. After “when” about the future, use the present simple: **when it arrives**, not “will arrive”.

q: Viết lại câu ở thể bị động (bắt đầu bằng “A new PIN…” hoặc “Every customer…”).
Rewrite the sentence in the passive (start with “A new PIN…” or “Every customer…”).
ex2.s: The bank sends a new PIN to every customer by post after they open an account.
a: A new PIN is sent to every customer by post after they open an account.
A new PIN is sent to every customer by post by the bank after they open an account.
Every customer is sent a new PIN by post after they open an account.
Every customer is sent a new PIN by post by the bank after they open an account.
e: Hiện tại đơn bị động: **is sent**. Có thể lấy tân ngữ gián tiếp làm chủ ngữ: Every customer **is sent** a new PIN. Thường bỏ “by the bank” vì đã rõ.
Present simple passive: **is sent**. The indirect object can be the subject: Every customer **is sent** a new PIN. “by the bank” is usually omitted.

ex2.s: Would it be possible|to send|this document|by express mail|so that|it arrives|in Da Lat|before Friday?
m: Có thể gửi tài liệu này bằng chuyển phát nhanh để nó đến Đà Lạt trước thứ Sáu được không?
Would it be possible to send this document by express mail so that it arrives in Da Lat before Friday?
e: **Would it be possible to + V?** là cách hỏi rất lịch sự. “so that + mệnh đề” chỉ mục đích.
**Would it be possible to + verb?** is a very polite request. “so that + clause” shows purpose.
f: Would it be possible to send

q: Viết email (80–100 từ) gửi ngân hàng báo mất thẻ: khi nào, ở đâu, yêu cầu khóa thẻ và cấp thẻ mới.
Write an email (80–100 words) to your bank reporting a lost card: when, where, and asking them to block it and issue a new one.
ex2.m:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to report that my debit card was lost yesterday afternoon, probably on the bus from the city centre to my office. My account number is 0123 4567. I would be grateful if you could block the card immediately so that it cannot be used by anyone else. Could you also tell me how long it will take for a new card to be sent to my home address? I would also like to know whether there is a fee for a replacement card.
Yours faithfully,
Tran Van An
e: Cần có: mở đầu & kết thư trang trọng; thời gian, địa điểm mất thẻ (bị động: was lost); yêu cầu lịch sự (I would be grateful if…, Could you…); ít nhất 1 câu hỏi gián tiếp.
Include: a formal greeting and closing; when and where the card was lost (passive: was lost); polite requests (I would be grateful if…, Could you…); at least one indirect question.

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Mệnh đề quan hệ**
• **who** (người), **which** (vật), **that** (người/vật – chỉ trong mệnh đề xác định), **where** (nơi chốn), **whose** (sở hữu).
• Xác định (không dấu phẩy): The film **that** I saw yesterday was great.
• Không xác định (có dấu phẩy, KHÔNG dùng that): The soundtrack, **which** was composed by a young pianist, is beautiful.
• Không lặp đại từ: the book which ~~it~~ made me cry.

**Grammar 1 – Relative clauses**
• **who** (people), **which** (things), **that** (people/things – defining clauses only), **where** (places), **whose** (possession).
• Defining (no commas): The film **that** I saw yesterday was great.
• Non-defining (commas, NO that): The soundtrack, **which** was composed by a young pianist, is beautiful.
• Don't repeat the pronoun: the book which ~~it~~ made me cry.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Tính từ -ed và -ing**
• **-ing** mô tả thứ gây ra cảm xúc: The film was **boring / moving / fascinating**.
• **-ed** mô tả cảm xúc của người: I was **bored / moved / fascinated**.
• Lỗi thường gặp: “I am boring” = Tôi là người nhàm chán (!) – muốn nói “Tôi chán” phải là **I am bored**.

**Grammar 2 – -ed and -ing adjectives**
• **-ing** describes the thing that causes the feeling: The film was **boring / moving / fascinating**.
• **-ed** describes how a person feels: I was **bored / moved / fascinated**.
• Common mistake: “I am boring” means people find you dull – to say how you feel, use **I am bored**.

**Phát âm – Đuôi -ed**
• /t/ sau âm vô thanh (k, p, s, ʃ, tʃ, f): shocked, impressed, relaxed.
• /d/ sau âm hữu thanh: bored, moved, surprised.
• /ɪd/ sau t, d: interested /ˈɪn.trɪs.tɪd/, disappointed, excited.
• Đừng thêm âm tiết thừa: moved là 1 âm tiết /muːvd/, không đọc “mu-vớt”.

**Pronunciation – -ed endings**
• /t/ after voiceless sounds (k, p, s, ʃ, tʃ, f): shocked, impressed, relaxed.
• /d/ after voiced sounds: bored, moved, surprised.
• /ɪd/ after t and d: interested /ˈɪn.trɪs.tɪd/, disappointed, excited.
• Don't add extra syllables: moved has one syllable /muːvd/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (25 phút): xem 1 trailer phim 3 lần – lần 3 bật phụ đề tiếng Anh, ghi 5 tính từ.
• Nói (20 phút): giới thiệu 1 bài hát yêu thích trong 1 phút dùng ít nhất 2 mệnh đề quan hệ.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 2 bài review phim ngắn, tìm các tính từ -ed/-ing.
• Viết (30 phút): viết review 80–100 từ cho một bộ phim, cuốn sách hoặc album.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học 15 từ về phim/sách/nhạc (plot, cast, chapter, lyrics…).

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (25 min): watch a film trailer 3 times – the third time with English subtitles – and note 5 adjectives.
• Speaking (20 min): present a favourite song in 1 minute using at least 2 relative clauses.
• Reading (20 min): read 2 short film reviews and find the -ed/-ing adjectives.
• Writing (30 min): write an 80–100-word review of a film, book or album.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn 15 words about films, books and music (plot, cast, chapter, lyrics…).

q: Vì sao người nói thích sách hơn phim?
Why does the speaker prefer the book?
o: Phim bỏ mất các chương giải thích lý do nhân vật rời nhà
The film left out chapters that explain why the hero leaves home
Sách có nhiều hình ảnh hơn
e: “the film left out the chapters which explain why the main character leaves home” – “leave out” = bỏ sót.
“the film left out the chapters which explain why the main character leaves home” – “leave out” = omit.

warm.s: I was so disappointed with the ending that I almost asked the cinema for my money back.
e: **disappointed** (-ed: cảm xúc của tôi), đọc đuôi /ɪd/. “so … that” = đến nỗi.
**disappointed** (-ed: my feeling), ending pronounced /ɪd/. “so … that” shows result.

warm.s: My favourite song is one which my mum used to sing to me when I was a child, so it always makes me feel calm.
e: Đọc liền mệnh đề quan hệ “one which my mum used to sing to me”; “used to” /ˈjuːs.tə/.
Say the relative clause “one which my mum used to sing to me” as one group; “used to” /ˈjuːs.tə/.

warm.s: I'd definitely recommend this series to anyone who likes gripping crime stories with a surprising twist at the end.
e: Nhấn “DEFinitely”, “recomMEND”, “GRIPping”. “twist” = tình tiết bất ngờ.
Stress “DEFinitely”, “recomMEND”, “GRIPping”. “twist” = an unexpected turn.

hard.s: Phim đó hay hơn mình tưởng nhiều – đến đoạn kết mình nổi cả da gà luôn.
a: That film was much better than I expected – the ending gave me goosebumps.
That film was way better than I expected – the ending gave me goosebumps.
That film was much better than I thought it would be – the ending gave me goosebumps.
The film was far better than I expected – the ending gave me goosebumps.
e: “hay hơn mình tưởng” = **better than I expected**; “nổi da gà” = **give sb goosebumps** – cách nói tự nhiên khi khen phim, nhạc.
“hay hơn mình tưởng” = **better than I expected**; “nổi da gà” = **give someone goosebumps** – a natural way to praise films or music.

q: Viết lại lời từ chối cho tự nhiên, dùng “… isn't really my thing”.
Rewrite the refusal more naturally using “… isn't really my thing”.
hard.s: I don't like jazz very much, so I don't want to come to the concert with you tonight.
a: Jazz isn't really my thing, so I don't want to come to the concert with you tonight.
Jazz is not really my thing, so I don't want to come to the concert with you tonight.
Jazz isn't really my thing, so I'd rather not come to the concert with you tonight.
e: **X isn't really my thing** là cách nói khéo “không hợp gu”, nghe mềm mỏng hơn “I don't like”.
**X isn't really my thing** is a soft, friendly way to say you don't enjoy something.

hard.s: I'd rather we watch a light comedy tonight, because I've had such a stressful day that I can't cope with anything scary.
a: I'd rather we watched a light comedy tonight, because I've had such a stressful day that I can't cope with anything scary.
I would rather we watched a light comedy tonight, because I've had such a stressful day that I can't cope with anything scary.
e: **I'd rather + chủ ngữ khác + quá khứ đơn** dù nói về hiện tại/tương lai: I'd rather we **watched**…
**I'd rather + another subject + past simple**, even about now or the future: I'd rather we **watched**…

hard.s: Please don't tell me what happens in the last episode – I haven't finished the series yet, so no ___, please!
a: spoilers
e: **spoiler** = thông tin tiết lộ nội dung; “No spoilers, please!” là câu rất hay dùng khi bàn về phim.
A **spoiler** reveals what happens; “No spoilers, please!” is very common when chatting about series.

rd2.tx: Last weekend I finally watched “The Quiet Garden”, a film which everyone in my class had been talking about. It's based on a novel that was written by a Japanese author in the 1990s. The story follows an old gardener who teaches a lonely teenage boy how to look after plants. At first I was a bit bored, because the beginning is very slow. However, the second half is really moving, and I was surprised by the ending, which I won't spoil here. The soundtrack, which was composed by a young pianist, is beautiful, and I've been listening to it all week. My only complaint is that some scenes are too dark, so it's hard to see the actors' faces. If you enjoy peaceful films that make you think, I'd definitely recommend it. I'm now reading the book, and so far it's even more fascinating than the film.
rd2.tr: Cuối tuần trước cuối cùng tôi cũng xem “Khu vườn yên tĩnh”, bộ phim mà cả lớp tôi đã bàn tán. Phim dựa trên một cuốn tiểu thuyết do một tác giả Nhật Bản viết vào những năm 1990. Câu chuyện kể về một người làm vườn già dạy một cậu thiếu niên cô đơn cách chăm sóc cây cối. Lúc đầu tôi hơi chán vì đoạn mở đầu rất chậm. Tuy nhiên, nửa sau thực sự cảm động, và tôi bất ngờ với cái kết – điều tôi sẽ không tiết lộ ở đây. Nhạc phim, do một nghệ sĩ dương cầm trẻ sáng tác, rất hay, và cả tuần nay tôi cứ nghe mãi. Điều duy nhất tôi không hài lòng là vài cảnh quá tối nên khó nhìn rõ mặt diễn viên. Nếu bạn thích những bộ phim nhẹ nhàng khiến bạn suy ngẫm, tôi chắc chắn sẽ giới thiệu phim này. Giờ tôi đang đọc cuốn sách, và đến giờ nó còn cuốn hút hơn cả bộ phim.

q: Vì sao lúc đầu người viết thấy chán?
Why was the writer bored at first?
e: “I was a bit bored, because the beginning is very slow.” Cái kết thì ngược lại – gây bất ngờ.
“I was a bit bored, because the beginning is very slow.” The ending, in contrast, was surprising.

q: Ai sáng tác nhạc phim?
Who composed the soundtrack?
o: Một nghệ sĩ dương cầm trẻ
e: Mệnh đề quan hệ “which was composed by a young pianist” bổ sung thông tin cho “The soundtrack”.
The relative clause “which was composed by a young pianist” adds information about “The soundtrack”.
f: which was composed by a young pianist

q: Người viết không hài lòng điều gì?
What is the writer's complaint?
e: “My only complaint is that some scenes are too dark” – không có lời chê về diễn xuất.
“My only complaint is that some scenes are too dark” – nothing is said against the acting.

ex2.s: The concert was so ___ that half of the audience left before the band had even finished their second song.
e: Buổi hòa nhạc **gây ra** cảm giác chán → tính từ **-ing**: boring. “bored” mô tả cảm xúc của khán giả.
The concert **causes** the feeling → **-ing** adjective: boring. “bored” describes how the audience felt.

ex2.s: My grandmother, ___ used to sing in a jazz band in Saigon, still remembers the words to hundreds of old songs.
a: who
e: Mệnh đề không xác định (có dấu phẩy) nói về người → **who**. Không dùng “that” sau dấu phẩy.
A non-defining clause (with commas) about a person → **who**. “that” is not used after a comma.

ex2.s: I was really interesting in the documentary about whales, so I watched it twice in one weekend and told all my friends about it.
a: I was really interested in the documentary about whales, so I watched it twice in one weekend and told all my friends about it.
e: Cảm xúc của người → **interested** (in). “I was interesting” nghĩa là “tôi thú vị”.
A person's feeling → **interested** (in). “I was interesting” means other people found you interesting.

ex2.s: This is the old cinema which I watched my very first film in 3D when I was eight years old.
a: This is the old cinema where I watched my very first film in 3D when I was eight years old.
This is the old cinema in which I watched my very first film in 3D when I was eight years old.
This is the old cinema that I watched my very first film in 3D in when I was eight years old.
e: Mệnh đề chỉ nơi chốn và đã có đủ tân ngữ (my first film) → dùng **where** (= in which).
The clause describes a place and already has an object (my first film), so use **where** (= in which).

ex2.s: Cuốn tiểu thuyết mà bạn cho tôi mượn tuần trước hay đến nỗi tôi đọc xong chỉ trong hai ngày.
a: The novel that you lent me last week was so good that I finished it in just two days.
The novel which you lent me last week was so good that I finished it in only two days.
The novel you lent me last week was so good that I finished it in just two days.
The novel you lent me last week was so good that I read it in just two days.
e: “mà bạn cho tôi mượn” = mệnh đề xác định (that/which, có thể bỏ). “hay đến nỗi” = **so good that**. Mượn: lend (cho mượn) ≠ borrow (đi mượn).
“mà bạn cho tôi mượn” is a defining clause (that/which, or no pronoun). “hay đến nỗi” = **so good that**. lend (give) ≠ borrow (take).
f: The novel that you lent me

ex2.s: Bộ phim này dựa trên một câu chuyện có thật về một cô gái đã đi bộ từ Hà Nội đến Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.
a: This film is based on a true story about a girl who walked from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City.
This movie is based on a true story about a girl who walked from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City.
This film is based on a true story about a girl that walked from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City.
e: “dựa trên” = **be based on** (bị động). Mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ người: **a girl who walked…**.
“dựa trên” = **be based on** (passive). Relative clause for a person: **a girl who walked…**.
f: is based on a true story

q: Nối hai câu bằng mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định (which).
Join the two sentences with a non-defining relative clause (which).
ex2.s: The music festival takes place every August. It attracts thousands of fans from all over Asia.
a: The music festival, which takes place every August, attracts thousands of fans from all over Asia.
The music festival, which attracts thousands of fans from all over Asia, takes place every August.
e: Mệnh đề không xác định đặt ngay sau danh từ, giữa hai dấu phẩy, dùng **which** (không dùng that).
Put the non-defining clause right after the noun, between commas, using **which** (not that).

ex2.s: I'd definitely recommend|this album|to anyone|who needs|some relaxing music|while they are|studying|for exams.
m: Tôi chắc chắn sẽ giới thiệu album này cho bất kỳ ai cần chút nhạc thư giãn khi ôn thi.
I'd definitely recommend this album to anyone who needs some relaxing music while they are studying for exams.
e: **recommend sth to sb**; “anyone who…” là mệnh đề quan hệ; “relaxing” (-ing) mô tả âm nhạc.
**recommend something to someone**; “anyone who…” is a relative clause; “relaxing” (-ing) describes the music.

rd.tx: Many adults believe they need long weekend classes to learn a language. However, research on memory suggests the opposite. Our brains remember information better when we review it several times over days or weeks, rather than all at once. This is called the spacing effect. For example, if you study twenty new words for ten minutes every day, you will probably remember more of them after a month than if you study for two hours every Sunday. Another useful habit is testing yourself instead of simply rereading your notes. When you try to recall a word, you strengthen the memory. So if you only have fifteen minutes a day, don't worry: as long as you practise regularly, you can still make real progress.
rd.tr: Nhiều người lớn tin rằng họ cần những lớp học dài vào cuối tuần để học ngoại ngữ. Tuy nhiên, nghiên cứu về trí nhớ cho thấy điều ngược lại. Não ghi nhớ tốt hơn khi ta ôn thông tin nhiều lần cách nhau vài ngày hoặc vài tuần, thay vì học dồn một lúc. Đó gọi là hiệu ứng giãn cách. Ví dụ, nếu bạn học 20 từ mới trong 10 phút mỗi ngày, sau một tháng bạn có lẽ sẽ nhớ được nhiều hơn so với học 2 tiếng mỗi Chủ nhật. Một thói quen hữu ích khác là tự kiểm tra thay vì chỉ đọc lại ghi chú. Khi cố nhớ lại một từ, bạn củng cố trí nhớ. Vì vậy nếu mỗi ngày chỉ có 15 phút, đừng lo: miễn là bạn luyện tập đều đặn, bạn vẫn tiến bộ thật sự.

rather than + -ing = instead of. “instead” alone can't introduce an -ing form (you need instead of); “as long as” means “provided that”, which doesn't fit.

You need a condition linker meaning “only if”: as long as (or provided that). The text uses exactly this: “as long as you practise regularly”.

a: Instead of simply rereading your notes, try to cover the page and recall each new word from memory before you check it.

After a preposition (instead of) the verb must be in the -ing form: rereading. Leaving the base form is a common mistake.

A first conditional (If + present simple, will + V) because it is a real possibility. “probably” goes after will. The comparison: more than if you study…
